subject: Next steps: deployment scenarios and sandbox sprint for NovaPay
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novapay.com>; Tom Harris <tom.harris@novapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + proposed sandbox sprint (hosted vs dedicated)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side:

- NovaPay priority: low-latency fraud scoring for transaction enrichment (avg payload ~120 tokens) and a daytime peak of ~350 reqs/sec with burst to ~1.2k for promotions. You mentioned data residency constraints for EU customers but the pilot targets US-only traffic.
- Deployment modes to evaluate: 1) Hosted API (fastest to get started, flexible endpoint map), 2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool for predictable tail latency), 3) Private VPC (if we need strict network isolation).

Suggested next actions:
1) 2-week sandbox sprint on Hosted API so your engineers can exercise endpoints + rate profiles (we can open a staging slice with prefetched KV cache).
2) If tail-latency / throughput from the sandbox suggests, we map to a Dedicated capacity estimate.
3) Procurement touchpoint for standard terms (I’ll loop procurement contacts into a later thread).

Deliverables we’ll provide if you approve the sprint: sandbox credentials, an endpoint/rate matrix tailored to your traffic, and a short playbook for prefix caching and batching recommendations.

Can we confirm a sandbox start on Monday, Feb 6th? If so I’ll share the access package and a short runbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood-sandbox-onramp.pdf (instructions), ratecaps-and-endpoint-matrix.csv

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novapay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@novapay.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed sandbox sprint (hosted vs dedicated)

Thanks Karthik — great call. A few clarifying items from our side:

- The traffic numbers are accurate. For pilot we only need US jurisdiction; full product would require EU residency for European customers.
- Data classification: most payloads are PII-lite (email, card last4 masked). We will need SOC2 evidence and basic E2E logging for the trial (non-production retention policy acceptable).
- Question: if we start on Hosted API, can we guarantee an endpoint per region and graceful automatic fallback to a compatible quantized model if capacity is limited? We want to avoid request errors during marketing bursts.

We’re okay to start Feb 6 for the sandbox. Can you include a sample endpoint map and the expected throttling behavior? Also please include any recommended prefetch/prefix cache settings for 120-token payloads.

I’ll loop procurement (procurement@novapay.com) if we need a quick quote for Dedicated later.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Integrations, NovaPay
elena.ruiz@novapay.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed sandbox sprint (hosted vs dedicated)

Elena — thanks, this is helpful. Short answers:

- Endpoint/residency: For the sandbox we’ll provision US-hosted endpoints only. Our Hosted API supports per-route region routing; for production we can expose region-specific endpoints (us / eu) or a single global endpoint with routing policies.
- Fallbacks: yes — Hosted supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants (e.g., int8-quantized) when a higher-capacity variant is unavailable; fallback behavior is configurable by policy (failover vs degrade).
- Throttling: sandbox slice will let you run up to 500 rps steady with brief bursts to 1.2k for short windows; sustained above 600 rps will be rate-limited. We’ll provide the exact ratecap table in the matrix.
- Prefix caching recommendation: for ~120-token inputs we suggest a 4–8 token prefix prefetch window and route-level KV cache TTL of 15 mins for session reuse patterns.

I’ll attach the endpoint/rate matrix and the onramp PDF now. Ben — can you confirm whether we should propose a Dedicated sizing delta upfront, or wait for sandbox telemetry?

—Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed sandbox sprint (hosted vs dedicated)

Looping in a quick recommendation:

- Start with Hosted sandbox telemetry before firming Dedicated sizing. The sandbox provides realistic tail latency signals and token-cost estimates.
- For procurement readiness: I recommend we prepare two ballpark options (Conservative Dedicated + Hybrid reserved burst) so procurement has an option set. I can draft this once we have 48 hours of sandbox metrics.

Monica — please kick off the sandbox provisioning and share credentials with Elena and Tom. Include the onramp PDF and the ratecaps CSV in the credential email.

—Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novapay.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@novapay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Feb 2028 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Sandbox access + kickoff checklist (NovaPay)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Welcome — sandbox slice is ready. Top-level items in this email: credentials, runbook links, and a quick checklist for the 2-week sprint.

Credentials (staging):
- API key: redwood-sbx-novapay-7f2c
- Staging endpoint: https://sbx-us.api.redwood.ai/v1/novapay

Attachments included: redwood-sandbox-onramp.pdf, ratecaps-and-endpoint-matrix.csv

2-week sprint kickoff checklist (suggested cadence):
1) Day 0: smoke test (10k tokens total) and validate auth + sample call
2) Days 1–2: load profile run to simulate 350 rps steady and short 1.2k burst windows
3) Days 3–5: collect latency histograms and KV cache hit rate; we’ll review on Day 6
4) Day 8: optional canary routing test with degraded quantized model to validate fallback behavior
5) Day 10–12: joint review of cost/latency trade-offs and Dedicated sizing recommendation

Two quick notes:
- Sandbox rate policy allows steady 500 rps and bursts to 1.2k for up to 1 min every 5 mins. Sustained bursts will return 429s.
- SOC2 evidence: we’ve shared the compliance packet in the HubSpot link; production onboarding will require an NDA + scoping call for audit copies.

When you’re ready I can book a 30-minute sync for Day 6 to review telemetry. Suggested times: Thurs 10:00am PT or Fri 2:00pm PT.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
